guidance.directive: Do not orchestrate phases via the Pi SDK. Phase orchestration MUST use `pi -p --mode json /skill:accord <phase> <ticket>` CLI subprocesses only; the SDK would roughly double the owned-code surface in unattended CI (session lifecycle, abort/signal handling, runtime/factory creation, bindExtensions) for limited gain. No `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` SDK symbol may be imported from `scripts/ci/`.

Do not distribute the autopipeline as a GitHub App. App installation requires hosted backend / webhook receiver per consumer org; a reusable workflow plus composite action gives consumers a 10-line opt-in with no central infrastructure on our side.

Do not distribute as a Docker action. Slower cold-start (image pull), harder for consumers to reproduce locally, worse iteration loop. The composite-action plus `scripts/ci/*.ts` approach is functionally equivalent and operationally cheaper.

Do not run a self-hosted webhook receiver for Jira events. Atlassian Automation natively supports `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/dispatches`; a self-hosted receiver adds operational burden, attack surface, and a single point of failure with zero behavioural benefit.

Do not auto-create follow-up Jira tickets when a phase returns `status: gaps`. Out of scope for v1 (deferred to v1.1). v1 only writes the structured `gaps[]` payload into a single terminal Jira comment (AC-10); authors decide whether to spawn follow-ups manually.

Do not write to Jira mid-run. No per-phase progress comments, no in-flight status transitions. Only terminal-state writes are permitted — the headless-agent contract requires a Jira comment to be an unambiguous terminal report.

Do not introduce a per-consumer prompt-level customisation surface for phase agents (e.g. swappable `phase-code` variants). v1 configuration surface is locked to `AGENTS.md` (`## Dev Harness` block) and `accord-config.json`; revisit for v2 once we have data on which prompts consumers most want to override.

Do not enable PR auto-merge after CI green. Compliance and SRE explicitly require human approval before an autonomous-agent commit lands on `main`. Auto-merge would change the trust contract; reviewers MUST remain in the loop. PRs may be opened as drafts where supported and never marked ready-for-review automatically.
